name: 2025-031 Opposition Brief v3.docx
preview: Attorney at Law · Morgan Law Office
SUPREME COURT OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK
COUNTY OF NEW YORK · Index No. —
MEMORANDUM OF LAW IN OPPOSITION TO DEFENDANT'S MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT

Plaintiff Paul Dawson submits this memorandum in opposition to the motion of Defendant Martin Distribution LLC for summary judgment. Defendant asks the Court to find that the exclusivity provision of the parties' agreement lapsed by course of dealing. The plain terms of the agreement foreclose that reading.

1. On April 4, 2022, Plaintiff and Defendant entered into an Exclusive Distribution Agreement covering the New York metropolitan area, for an initial term of three years, renewing automatically (Exhibit 4).
2. Beginning in September 2024, Defendant stopped filling Plaintiff's purchase orders and began supplying a competing retailer in the same territory (Exhibits 7 to 9).
3. By letter dated February 12, 2025, Plaintiff demanded that Defendant honor the exclusivity provision (Exhibit 10). Defendant did not respond.

I. The exclusivity provision did not lapse. Section 4 of the Agreement requires any termination of exclusivity to be given by written notice, delivered by certified mail at least six months before the renewal date. Defendant never gave that notice. The Agreement therefore renewed on April 4, 2025, on the same terms, exclusivity included.
II. Plaintiff suffered lost profits. The purchase orders left unfilled between September 2024 and March 2025 represent lost gross profits of $86,400 (Exhibit 12, accountant's report).

Article VII — Restrictions on transfer of shares

7.1 No stockholder may sell, assign or transfer any shares of the Corporation, including to another stockholder, without the prior written consent of the Board of Directors, given by a two-thirds vote.

name: 2026-015 Memo on right of first refusal.docx
preview: Attorney at Law · Morgan Law Office
Right of first refusal in the stockholders agreement
You asked whether the stockholders agreement should include a right of first refusal in addition to the transfer restrictions in Article VII of the bylaws.

Yes. The board consent requirement lets the company block an unwanted buyer; a right of first refusal lets the existing stockholders buy the shares first, at the price offered by the third party. The two work together.
Right of first refusal for each stockholder, pro rata to its holding, exercisable within 30 days of notice.
Price: the bona fide third-party offer, or, failing agreement, fair market value set by an independent appraiser.

name: Research - notice of appeal deadline for family court orders.docx
preview: Appeal from a family court order
Question: how long does a party have to file a notice of appeal from a family court order setting temporary custody and support?
Answer: 30 days from service of the order with notice of entry (CPLR 5513(a); Family Court Act § 1113). The order remains in effect while the appeal is pending unless a stay is granted.
To check: whether the order was served with notice of entry, or only mailed by the clerk; the 30 days run from service.
